newsitem.title: USA: Compass to buy Daka for $195 million.
newsitem.headline: Compass to buy Daka for $195 million.

text.p: Compass Group PLC said Wednesday its Compass Holdings Inc. unit has a definitive agreement to buy the contract foodservice business of Daka International in a deal worth about $195 million.

Compass, a world leader in the field with head offices in England and Wales, said it will pay about $85 million to Daka stockholders through a cash tender offer of $7.50 per share. It will use $110 million to repay Daka debt.
Daka stockholders will also receive shares of a new company that will own all of Daka's non-foodservice business, which Compass will not acquire.
Compass said Daka, based in Danvers, Mass., will first spin off its restaurant business to its shareholders, and then Compass will make a cash tender offer for all of Daka's common shares.
After the tender offer, Compass will merge Daka with one of its subsidiaries.
Compass plans to finance the deal, which is subject to approval by regulators and Daka shareholders, with funds from established cash sources.
Compass, whose U.S. head office is in Charlotte, N.C., employs about 120,000 people worldwide.
Daka operates in the contract foodservice management industry and the restaurant industry.
Daka's stock rose $1.25 to $12.50 early on Nasdaq.
